hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Sudan on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Sudan on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Khartoum?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Sudan is Khartoum.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Sudan about 1,878,000 square kilometres; Chad about 1,284,000 square kilometres; Nigeria about 923,768 square kilometres; Lebanon about 10,452 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Sudan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sudan article.

questions.proof: Its capital and largest city is Khartoum.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Sudan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Sudan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Sudan article.

questions.proof: Sudan borders Egypt to the north, Eritrea and Ethiopia to the east, South Sudan to the south, the Central African Republic to the southwest, Chad to the west, and Libya to the northwest.
